cases.scenario: 34% of accounts have no employee count. The existing fit model scores a missing employee count as zero points.
pass_if: States that missing is not low and that zero-scoring penalises under-covered segments
Names the coverage bias: small, non-US, privately held and recently founded companies
Prescribes scoring on known attributes normalised to the achievable maximum, plus a confidence flag
Distinguishes a genuine zero from a missing value explicitly
Reports coverage per attribute and by segment, and states the direction of error on affected grades
fail_if: Drops accounts with missing attributes without stating the bias introduced

cases.scenario: The stated ICP is enterprise manufacturing. Evidence shows mid-market services wins at 31% versus 13%, with non-overlapping intervals, but enterprise deals are much larger.
pass_if: Reports both the stated ICP and the evidence side by side with the verdict per attribute
Gives win rates with intervals and sample sizes
Names the deal-size trade explicitly rather than declaring the data the winner
Raises the legitimate reasons the stated ICP might still be right: deliberate strategy change, selection effect, value over volume
Leaves the decision with the business while making the evidence unambiguous
fail_if: Declares the stated ICP wrong with no consideration of strategy or deal value
Reports win rates without sample sizes or intervals

cases.scenario: A team proposes a single 0-100 lead score blending firmographic fit and engagement activity.
pass_if: Rejects the collapse and explains that a high-fit unengaged account and a low-fit engaged account are opposite situations
Names the action for each quadrant
Prescribes the two-axis grid rendering
Notes that a combined model downstream is acceptable provided both components stay visible

cases.scenario: A firmographic level has 6 opportunities and 4 wins. A stakeholder wants to add it to the ICP as a 67% win-rate segment.
pass_if: Reports the counts and marks the level insufficient evidence against the volume floor
Gives the confidence interval, which will be very wide, rather than only refusing
States that the level is not dropped, just unproven, and names the volume that would settle it
Does not add the level to the criteria on this evidence
fail_if: Reports 67% as a win rate for the segment
Drops the level silently from the analysis

cases.scenario: Two enrichment providers disagree on employee band for 30% of accounts. Grades built on the blend are being disputed by sales.
pass_if: Reports the conflict rate as a measured number
Explains the cause: providers use different entity definitions, legal entity versus group versus network headcount
Prescribes one provider per attribute or an explicit priority order with the winning provider recorded
Recommends banding rather than raw values to absorb provider disagreement
Acknowledges that sales is right to distrust a grade built on an unnormalised blend
fail_if: Continues using the blend with no normalisation

cases.scenario: 47% of the database is graded A. Weekly capacity is about 200 accounts.
pass_if: States plainly that a grade covering 47% of the database is not a filter
Derives a capacity-based cut and reports the resulting A/B win-rate separation
Checks whether the grades separate outcomes with non-overlapping intervals
Distinguishes grade inflation from genuine improvement by checking whether win rate moved with the distribution
fail_if: Tightens the cut without reporting the effect on separation
Reads a rightward distribution shift as improving lead quality without checking outcomes
